Signal Kit

A UI kit that rebuilds the sage, coral and stripe poster style from code. Everything on this page is drawn with CSS and vector glyphs. There are no bitmaps. English leads, with Japanese and French woven in sparingly. The same parts ship as SwiftUI views in ios/.

[ assessment / open-design brutalist-skill ]

The repo skill is a 9 KB text prompt with no assets, shapes or code. It also contradicts this poster. It bans rounded corners, but the poster is built on stadium pills and rounded X marks. It allows one light or dark background per screen, but the poster puts sage slabs on an ink ground. Its accent is hazard red #E61919, not coral #ff715e.

Its spirit is still useful: grids, mono telemetry text and technical framing. So this kit is built from scratch. It has its own tokens, generated glyphs, web components and SwiftUI shapes, all measured off the reference.

01

Poster study

reference rebuilt 1:1 in layout from kit primitives · 1333 × 2000 vector · brand copy swapped for placeholders

Nested stadium pill

Three stacked capsules and a slot line. Proportions: band 18% of height, core 15%, slot 3%. Doubles as a hero, card, scrubber or progress bar. .pill · NestedPill()

Rounded X

The union of two crossed stadiums. It comes outlined, solid or faint. Use it for status, done or rest days, close and error. #g-x-line · RoundedX()

Stripe field

A soft repeating gradient with a 6 pt period. Facets are extra layers with a different angle and a clip-path. .tex .facet · StripeField (Canvas)

Slab and coral diagonal

Screens split into an ink top and a sage bottom along one diagonal. The coral band is the only accent surface. .slab .band · DiagonalSlab

Chamfer frame

A hairline outline with two cut corners. It frames fields, groups and ID cards. .chamfer · ChamferRect()

Instrument badges

The topo disc, record rings, radar fan, barcode lines, crosshair and arrows. All are generated, so they recolor with tokens. assets/svg/*

AXIOMsp c53

Type pair

Archivo Expanded Black for the wordmark, Archivo Medium with tight tracking for labels, and JetBrains Mono for right-aligned telemetry. All are OFL and bundled for iOS.

09

Numbering and hex labels

Entry numbers, #hex callouts, 200 ppi specs and rules that end in a block. Use real values from your app, never filler.

05

Three languages

english · 日本語 · français
EN

English runs the interface

Every action, label and number. If someone has to read it to use the app, it's in English.

Protected
日本語

Japanese adds texture

Vertical captions along edges, seal stamps and outlined display kanji. Use one Japanese moment per screen at most. It is never the only label on a control.

認証受信箱圏外
Fr.

French is the aside

Italic footnotes, dates, taglines and pull quotes. Use it once per screen at most, usually in the quietest spot.

« celui qu'on n'entend pas »
×3

All three only once

Stack the same line in all three languages in one place only: the lock screen, splash or about page. Repeating the stack elsewhere weakens it.
